   "source": [
    "# Parameter sweeps and persistence\n",
    "\n",
    "A sweep builds one cavity per parameter combination, each with its own folder and\n",
    "simulations, so a whole family of designs is analysed and compared in a few lines. It is a\n",
    "`Study` operation (every point is a distinct, separately-saved cavity). We then show that a\n",
    "saved study reloads from disk — cached results come back with no re-simulation, so you can\n",
    "compare runs made in different sessions."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "afc94ecc",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-20T21:39:02.401739Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-20T21:39:02.401542Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-20T21:39:04.393621Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-20T21:39:04.392663Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import tempfile\n",
    "\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "from cavsim2d import Study, Pillbox\n",
    "from cavsim2d.utils.style import apply_style, WARM\n",
    "\n",
    "apply_style()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "673f4d37",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. A tensor sweep\n",
    "\n",
    "`study.sweep(template, {var: values}, mode='tensor')` sweeps every combination of the\n",
    "given values (a cartesian grid). Each point is `template.rebuild(...)` with the swept\n",
    "variables overridden, so it works for any model and any variable — a multicell `'Req'` would\n",
    "correctly set every cell."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "5bc209b8",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {

   ],
   "source": [
    "study = Study(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'sweep_demo'))\n",
    "template = Pillbox(1, [100, 100, 20, 0, 50], beampipe='both')\n",
    "\n",
    "sw = study.sweep(template, {'Req': [95, 100, 105], 'Ri': [18, 20]}, mode='tensor')\n",
    "print(f'{len(sw.cavities_list)} cavities (3 x 2 grid)')\n",
    "sw.sweep_table"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d9f1382a",

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0b6aa508",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 2. Compare\n",
    "\n",
    "With the joined table, comparisons are a groupby. Here, frequency against equator radius for\n",
    "each aperture:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "b2f558d1",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.029257Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.029097Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.153758Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.152686Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))\n",
    "for i, (ri, grp) in enumerate(res.groupby('Ri')):\n",
    "    g = grp.sort_values('Req')\n",
    "    ax.plot(g['Req'], g['freq [MHz]'], 'o-', color=WARM[1 + 2 * i], label=f'Ri = {ri} mm')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('equator radius Req [mm]')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('frequency [MHz]')\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "ax.set_title('Pillbox fundamental across the sweep')\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "614990af",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The built-in study comparison plots work too, since a sweep *is* a study.\n",
    "`plot_compare` draws each cavity as a point per figure of merit (and, with `uq=True`,\n",
    "its error bar), labelled by the sweep point it came from:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "c2eb3134",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.156368Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.156139Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.607158Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.606396Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x300 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "sw.eigenmode.plot_compare(qois=['freq [MHz]', 'R/Q [Ohm]'])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e989cadb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 3. Hadamard (element-wise) sweep\n",
    "\n",
    "`mode='hadamard'` pairs the value lists element-wise instead of taking the full grid — so\n",
    "`{'Req': [98, 102], 'Ri': [19, 21]}` gives just two cavities, `(98, 19)` and `(102, 21)`. Every\n",
    "value list must therefore be the same length; an unequal set is rejected."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "acfce3ac",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.608788Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.608604Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.616432Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-20T21:39:22.615901Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "hadamard cavities: ['Req98_Ri19', 'Req102_Ri21']\n",
      "unequal lengths rejected: hadamard sweep requires every parameter value list to be the same length; got {'Req': 3, 'Ri': 2}. Use mode=\"tensor\" for a full grid.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "sw_h = study.sweep(template, {'Req': [98, 102], 'Ri': [19, 21]}, mode='hadamard')\n",
    "print('hadamard cavities:', [c.name for c in sw_h.cavities_list])\n",
    "\n",
    "try:\n",
    "    study.sweep(template, {'Req': [98, 102, 106], 'Ri': [19, 21]}, mode='hadamard')\n",
    "except ValueError as e:\n",
    "    print('unequal lengths rejected:', e)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f4de7d33",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 4. Persistence — reload a saved study\n",
    "\n",
    "Every cavity saved its geometry and results to disk. `Study.load(project_dir)` reconstructs the\n",
    "whole collection — each cavity the right type, pointing at its existing folder — so all cached\n",
    "results (`eigenmode`, `wakefield`, `tuned`) read straight back with no re-simulation."
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "bcde7c17",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {

    }
   },

     "execution_count": 7,

   ],
   "source": [
    "reloaded = Study.load(sw.projectDir)\n",
    "print(f'reloaded {len(reloaded.cavities_list)} cavities: '\n",
    "      f'{[type(c).__name__ for c in reloaded.cavities_list][:1]} ...')\n",
    "\n",
    "# cached QOIs come straight off disk — no solver runs here\n",
    "again = reloaded.results('eigenmode')\n",
    "again[['freq [MHz]', 'R/Q [Ohm]']].round(2)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2a373cf4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Because a loaded study behaves like any other, two studies from different sessions (or a\n",
    "loaded one against a freshly-built one) compare directly — `study.eigenmode.plot_compare()`,\n",
    "`study.eigenmode.qois_df`, or by joining their `results()` tables. See the\n",
    "[configuration](../../configuration) and [concepts](../../concepts) guides for the folder\n",
    "layout the persistence relies on."
   ]
  }
